cells.tense: You are here at the pen, and your sense of what's fair is speaking while you still hold it.
cells.ask: Offer to gather what this stretch of change actually grew, and let the right moment to take it in find you instead of forcing it.
cells.core:
You have a working compass. Something is fair or it isn't, and you know which without doing sums. In this part of your life that shows up as a clean pull toward what you actually want — you can tell which direction is yours and which one you've borrowed, and the borrowed ones don't hold. You've also learned to wait on your own timing. The ending came, the new thing started, and you let the fruit set before you picked it. That patience is not passivity. It's you trusting that what you've been through has a yield.

There is more gathered here than you've stopped to count. Taking stock — carefully, at your pace, without rushing the season — is the next thing your compass is free to feed. You are not behind. You are standing in the middle of a harvest that hasn't fully announced itself yet.
cells.sheetLine: You feel what's fair, and you're letting what you've grown come ripe in its own time.
cells.verb: weighing what's fair and what's owed by feel alone
cells.place: the pull toward what you actually want, recognized rather than handed to you

cells.tense: You're braced far ahead, weighing accounts that haven't come due yet.
cells.ask: Let one thing you've already decided be someone else's to hold for a day — strength that contains instead of proves.
cells.core:
A live sense of fairness is a gift — you feel the right shape of a thing before anyone explains it, and in this part of your life that means you can tell which pull is yours before you can argue for it. But right now you're running the whole ledger ahead of time. Every future exchange gets weighed before it happens, every debt pre-counted, every slight balanced in advance against a score no one else is keeping. The bracing burns the energy the fairness needs.

Support is what's missing, not vigilance. Hand the weight of one thing — a decision, a worry, a keeping-track — to someone whose strength can hold it beside you. Holding without forcing is the way back.
cells.sheetLine: You're keeping accounts that haven't opened yet, and the tally is spending you.
cells.verb: weighing what's fair and what's owed by feel alone
cells.place: the pull toward what you actually want, recognized rather than handed to you

cells.tense: You stopped at a door that's already behind you, and you're still standing where you stopped.
cells.ask: Follow one practiced step today, and let it carry you toward the light you'd stopped walking toward.
cells.core:
The compass never stopped working. You can still feel the difference between fair and unfair the way you feel warmth — it's just that somewhere along the way you stopped acting from it, and stopped letting the pull toward what you want move you. The direction is still there, remembered, not arrived at; you're just not walking.

What's starved is the moving, not the knowing. One small, disciplined step — a practice followed, a direction honored once — sends power back up into the part of you that points at what you want. You don't have to force feeling into a place that's gone quiet. Take the step and let the pull follow.
cells.sheetLine: The compass works fine. It's the walking toward the light that stopped.
cells.verb: weighing what's fair and what's owed by feel alone
cells.place: the pull toward what you actually want, recognized rather than handed to you

cells.tense: Your hand is already on a page you haven't admitted you're writing.
cells.ask: Pick the single thing you already know is right, and say it was your call to know it.
cells.core:
You are already steering by your own sense of what's fair — the pulls you follow, the things you quietly won't do, the way you tilt toward one light and away from another. None of that is luck or circumstance. But when it comes up, you describe it as the situation, the timing, what anyone would do. The compass runs; you just don't claim the hand on it.

What's needed is smaller than you'd think. One truth you already carry, taken as yours — no argument, no proof needed, just the plain acknowledgment that you're the one who knows it. Direct perception lands without a fight. Let one of its perceptions land as yours.
cells.sheetLine: You already know what's right here. You're just calling it the situation.

cells.place: the pull toward what you actually want, recognized rather than handed to you
